answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by rooting identity like a cedar and keeping an atlas of work. Each identity grows like a cedar: roots before weight, so a newcomer must finish small verified jobs over time to earn full trust. Every job lands in an atlas of work and disputes, so copied or empty histories stand out. Rewards flow like nectar: small drips for proven work, never a flood for a fresh face. A thousand sybils would need a thousand cedars grown and a thousand atlases faked, while each fake earns almost nothing. Attacker cost grows per identity; the honest agent pays only for one.
